resources.string: Live shooting coach · advice only
Searching for a supported subject. Use good light and keep the subject visible; an undetected subject has no reliable framing location.
Subject target is near the edge. Leave more space around it; full subject bounds are not measured.
Subject target is near a vertical third. Keep space in the direction it faces.
Try moving the subject toward a vertical third, or centre it for a symmetric scene.
Keep the likely action inside the frame. For action, consider 1/500 s if supported; motion is not measured.
Use a tripod. Expose the stationary background first and leave room for moving lights. Keep white balance fixed across sources.
Use a tripod. Frame moving water or clouds with a stable reference. Lower source exposure if highlights clip; averaging cannot restore them.
Brace the phone or use a tripod. Keep subjects still; use the lowest ISO that permits a suitable source exposure.
Use a tripod, focus on a distant star and avoid bright foreground lights. Long exposures need lens and camera support; inspect stars for trailing.
Fix the phone on a tripod. Include a stable foreground and allow sky space for trails. Keep focus, framing and white balance fixed.
Keep framing steady and avoid moving subjects. Use unlocked automatic ISO and shutter for exposure bracketing. Watch the bright end of the histogram.
Keep the subject within the frame across the sequence. For action consider 1/500 s if supported; processing may limit cadence.
Choose a static detailed subject. Hold steadily with only natural small movement; avoid panning and keep focus fixed. More pixels require independent samples.
For a still portrait, consider about 1/125 s; for action about 1/500 s if supported. Adjust ISO to suit the light. Subject motion is not measured.

Detected subject bounds are close to an edge. Leave more room around the subject, especially above the head.
ISO starting point: %1$d, estimated from current exposure. Check brightness and noise.

Focus manually on a distant star using magnification; check the smallest sharp point.
Focus on the main subject, then lock focus for a static stack.
Use continuous AF for a moving subject; tap the intended subject if detection chooses another.
